title: Local Frobenius under pullback of constructible rational Weil sheaves
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, an algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a morphism of separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and let $f:X_0\times_{k_0}k\to Y_0\times_{k_0}k$ be its base change. Use the common-stage rational coefficient categories and constructible Weil sheaves of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], and derived pullback of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For every constructible $\Qlb$-Weil sheaf $\mathcal F$ on $Y_0$, the pullback $Lf^*\mathcal F$, with its induced Weil structure, lies in the constructible heart. Write it as $f^*\mathcal F$. For every closed point $z\in X_0$, the point $x=f_0(z)$ is closed, $\kappa(x)\subset\kappa(z)$ is a finite extension of positive degree $e$, and $q_z=q_x^e$, where $q_t=\#\kappa(t)$. For compatible geometric points there is a natural $\Qlb$-linear isomorphism
$$c_{f,z}:(f^*\mathcal F)_{\bar z}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal F_{\bar x},\qquad c_{f,z}F_{z,f^*\mathcal F}=F_{x,\mathcal F}^{\,e}c_{f,z},$$
where the local operators are geometric Frobenius as in [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]. In particular the eigenvalue multiset at $z$ is $\{\alpha^e:\alpha\in\operatorname{Eig}(F_{x,\mathcal F})\}$, with algebraic multiplicities.

source.place: Step 2, sentence explaining the eigenvalues alpha^e lambda. This is the rational, morphism-functorial input needed there; the cited finite-coefficient trace formula does not itself state it. Compare the concrete realization in WeilConjectures/WeilSheaf/StalkUpperStar.lean:333–358 and StalkCharpoly.lean:588–625; no identification of that concrete category with the common-stage category is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact] with $h=f$ and $\Lambda=\Qlb$. Its categories, standard heart and derived pullback are precisely those in the item, so $Lf^*\mathcal F$ lies in the constructible heart. The same statement applies at every finite coefficient-field stage and to geometric-point pullbacks. The canonical comparison $\beta_1:Lg_X^*Lf^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*Lg_Y^*$ comes from $fg_X=g_Yf$ and the composition isomorphisms of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], rationalized and used stagewise as in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus the induced Weil structure is $\theta_X=Lf^*(\theta_Y)\beta_1$; it is an isomorphism, so this heart object is a Weil sheaf.

source.place: Step 2: rational pullback and the residue-degree Frobenius formula

proof.text: Let $z$ be closed and put $x=f_0(z)$. By [lem-kun-closed-point-field](a), $\kappa(z)$ is finite over $k_0$. The scheme morphism gives a $k_0$-embedding $\kappa(x)\hookrightarrow\kappa(z)$, so $\kappa(x)$ is also finite over $k_0$. The converse in that same criterion makes $x$ closed. Set $d=[\kappa(x):k_0]\geq1$ and $e=[\kappa(z):\kappa(x)]\geq1$. A basis in each field extension gives $[\kappa(z):k_0]=de$, and counting coordinate tuples in a basis gives $q_z=q^{de}=(q^d)^e=q_x^e$.

source.place: Step 2: rational pullback and the residue-degree Frobenius formula

proof.text: Work over one finite coefficient field $E$ defining $M=\operatorname{For}\mathcal F$, its Weil isomorphism $\theta$ and its inverse. Such a stage exists: represent these finitely many arrows in the Hom colimits of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], then enlarge until both inverse equations hold. Choose compatible points $\bar z:s\to X$ and $\bar x=f\bar z:s\to Y$. Write $J_z=\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar z^*$ and $J_x=\operatorname{Fib}_sL\bar x^*$. The inverse of the composition isomorphism $L(f\bar z)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}L\bar z^*Lf^*$, followed by $\operatorname{Fib}_s$, is a natural isomorphism $c_M:J_zLf^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}J_xM$. Use the canonical families of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]: they are defined for all derived-complete constructible objects without a finite Tor-amplitude condition, give composition isomorphisms after rationalization, and commute with scalar comparisons. Applying also [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] shows that $c_M$ commutes with finite coefficient extension, including its identity and tower identifications. Thus $c_M$ defines a natural $\Qlb$-linear comparison on the common-stage category. Its degree-zero map is the desired stalk isomorphism.

source.place: Step 2: rational pullback and the residue-degree Frobenius formula

proof.text:
Here is the Frobenius compatibility of this comparison at stage $E$. Put $G_Y=Lg_Y^*$ and $G_X=Lg_X^*$. For $n$ divisible by $de$, both points return: $g_X^n\bar z=\bar z g_s^n$ and $g_Y^n\bar x=\bar x g_s^n$. Let $t^X_{n,N}:J_zN\to J_zG_X^nN$ and $t^Y_{n,M}:J_xM\to J_xG_Y^nM$ be the point transports of [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization]. Let $\beta_n:G_X^nLf^*\to Lf^*G_Y^n$ be the comparison from $fg_X^n=g_Y^nf$. Naturality of the iterated point transport applied to $L\bar z^*Lf^*M\cong L\bar x^*M$, followed by the associative composition identifications, gives
$$c_{G_Y^nM}\,J_z(\beta_n)\,t^X_{n,Lf^*M}=t^Y_{n,M}\,c_M.$$
The naturality used here is [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural](2), iterated $n$ times; the two rebracketings agree by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. This constructs the equation in the rational category itself, rather than importing a finite-ring stalk equation.

source.place: Step 2: rational pullback and the residue-degree Frobenius formula

proof.text:
The induced iterated Weil structure is $\theta_X^{[n]}=Lf^*(\theta_Y^{[n]})\beta_n$: induct on $n$, substituting $\theta_X=Lf^*(\theta_Y)\beta_1$ and using naturality and associativity of the composition comparisons in [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For $n=de$, the preceding equation and naturality of $c$ for $\theta_Y^{[n]}$ therefore give
$$\begin{aligned}
c_MJ_z(\theta_X^{[n]})t^X_{n,Lf^*M}
&=J_x(\theta_Y^{[n]})c_{G_Y^nM}J_z(\beta_n)t^X_{n,Lf^*M}\\
&=J_x(\theta_Y^{[n]})t^Y_{n,M}c_M.
\end{aligned}$$
By [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], the left operator is $c_MF_z$ and the right one is the $q^{de}$-return operator at $x$, followed by $c_M$.

source.place: Step 2: rational pullback and the residue-degree Frobenius formula

proof.text:
To identify that return operator, keep the point $\bar x$ fixed and put $J=J_x$, $G=G_Y$, $A=\theta_Y^{[d]}:G^dM\to M$, and $t_{rd,N}=t^Y_{rd,N}$. Splitting the defining list of $(r+1)d$ point transports after the first $rd$ entries gives
$$t_{(r+1)d,N}=t_{d,G^{rd}N}\,t_{rd,N}.$$
This equality uses the same return $g_Y^d\bar x=\bar xg_s^d$ and associative comparisons of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Naturality of the $d$-fold transport [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural] gives $JG^d(\theta^{[rd]})t_{d,G^{rd}M}=t_{d,M}J(\theta^{[rd]})$. Since the definition of iterated Weil structure gives $\theta^{[(r+1)d]}=A\,G^d(\theta^{[rd]})$, we obtain
$$J(\theta^{[(r+1)d]})t_{(r+1)d,M}=(J(A)t_{d,M})(J(\theta^{[rd]})t_{rd,M}).$$
Starting with $r=1$, induction shows that the $ed$-return operator is $(J(A)t_{d,M})^e=F_x^e$, with exactly the geometric-Frobenius convention of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].

source.place: Step 2: rational pullback and the residue-degree Frobenius formula

proof.text:
The equality just proved is compatible with change of the finite field $E$. Indeed the scalar/composition equation of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization] identifies the two scalar extensions of $c$ and $\beta_n$; the explicit scalar equation in [lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization] identifies those of $t_{n,M}$; and naturality identifies those of $\theta^{[n]}$. Consequently extension to any common larger field sends every factor in the displayed equations to its corresponding factor. With [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] these give the same $\Qlb$-linear equation on the common-stage fibres, independently of representatives:
$$c_{f,z}F_{z,f^*\mathcal F}=F_{x,\mathcal F}^{e}c_{f,z}.$$
Taking degree-zero cohomology is legitimate by the point-fibre clause of [lem-a1-constructible-pullback-t-exact].

source.place: Step 2: rational pullback and the residue-degree Frobenius formula

proof.text: The two endomorphisms are conjugate after replacing $F_x$ by $F_x^e$. Over the algebraically closed coefficient field choose an upper triangular matrix for $F_x$. Its diagonal lists its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity; the diagonal of its $e$-th power lists their $e$-th powers, with repetitions retained even when distinct eigenvalues acquire the same power. Conjugation preserves the characteristic polynomial, proving the asserted multiset formula. The empty diagonal covers the zero sheaf.
